newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serb opposition to widen protests.
newsitem.headline: Serb opposition to widen protests.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders, vowing to widen their wave of protest over local election results, are calling on President Slobodan Milosevic to quit.

Vuk Draskovic, one of the leaders of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition, told a crowd in central Belgrade on Wednesday the issue was no longer Milosevic's refusal to accept opposition victories.
"Until yesterday we fought to protect our election victory. Now the goal of our rebellion is the resignation of Slobodan Milosevic," Draskovic declared.
Another opposition leader, Zoran Djindjic, declared: "Every day we are pulling a brick from his (Milosevic's) Chinese Wall."
Zajedno has led more than a week of demonstrations since the authorities annulled results of a municipal poll which went badly for Milosevic's ruling Socialists.

An estimated 50,000 to 80,000 opposition supporters marched through central Belgrade on Wednesday. It was one of the largest demonstations since Zajedno victories were overturned in 15 of Serbia's 18 biggest towns.
Large numbers of workers have joined similar rallies in Nis and Kragujevac, industrial towns once Milosevic strongholds.
In the neigbouring republic of Monetenegro -- Serbia's only remaining partner in the Yugoslav federation -- the opposition organised rallies in support of Zajedno.
Djnidjic told Reuters that Zajedno activists were working with unions on the prospects for strikes and civil disobedience.
"If the workers join us we will ask for Slobodan Milosevic's head," Djindjic said.

Re-run elections took place on Wednesday in cities where second-round results 10 days ago were overturned. The opposition called for boycott and there were no figures for the turnout. Results were expected on Thursday.
State televison and newspapers controlled by Milosevic heaped scorn on the opposition and portrayed protesters as an anarchic mob.
Showing footage of broken windows, a television presenter said: "These are only some of the consequences of their vandalism in the name of democracy."
